one_liner: Parallel Rust replacement for du -sh that prints one directory total; author measured 10x faster cold-cache, 2.2x warm.
what_it_does: diskus walks one or more directory trees and prints only their combined size, like du -sh (disk usage, st_blocks x 512) or du -sb with -b (apparent size). It is a CLI plus a small Rust library (DiskUsage::new(paths).apparent_size().count(), returning a size and a list of traversal errors). There is no per-directory breakdown, no depth option, and no exclude patterns.
how_it_is_fast: It runs symlink_metadata (lstat) and read_dir calls in parallel on a rayon thread pool sized at 3x the CPU count (capped at 64), recursing with into_par_iter over each directory's children, and sends sizes over a crossbeam channel to one summing thread. Oversubscribing threads keeps many metadata requests in flight so the kernel I/O scheduler can reorder them on a cold cache; GNU du issues them one at a time. Hard links are counted once through a (device, inode) HashSet, but only for files with nlink > 1.
when_to_use: Getting one total size for a large tree (hundreds of thousands of files) on SSD/NVMe with a cold page cache, where serial du stalls on metadata latency
Scripts and prompts that only need a byte count: output switches to a bare number when piped
Multi-core machines; the default 3x-cores worker count was tuned for both cold and warm caches
Embedding a fast parallel du-style total in a Rust program through the library API
when_not_to_use: Small trees: issue #38 reports diskus 115.8 ms vs du -sch 22.8 ms on a ~4.5 GB build directory, because thread-pool startup dominates
Very deep directory nesting: open issue #27 (since 2019) reports a stack overflow from the recursive walk
When you need a per-subdirectory breakdown, depth limits, excludes or interactive browsing (use pdu, gdu, dust or ncdu)
When you need to stay on one filesystem or follow symlinks: no -x / one-file-system option, and following symlinks is an open request (#44)
Windows totals that must not double count: hard links and junctions are counted multiple times there by design

integration.dependencies: rayon 1.11, crossbeam-channel 0.5; clap, humansize, num-format for the CLI feature
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.80 per Cargo.toml rust-version (README still says 1.76)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, Haiku and other Unix (packages for Debian, Arch, Void, Homebrew, MacPorts, NixOS)
integration.thread_safety: Library call spawns its own rayon pool and receiver thread per count(); no shared global state documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — matches du -sh / du -sb totals for a path, but supports none of du's other flags

gotchas: Default count is disk usage (since v0.6); -b switches to apparent size, and v0.9.0 changed whether directory entries are counted to match du, so totals from older versions differ
Errors (unreadable directories, missing metadata) are hidden unless --verbose is passed, so a permission problem silently shrinks the total
Spawns up to 64 threads by default; on shared or throttled hosts pass --threads (-j) explicitly
Hard-link deduplication keeps a HashSet of every multi-link inode in memory
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick diskus over pdu, gdu or zdu when you want only a single total from the smallest tool; the gdu README itself notes diskus is faster at that, while pdu and gdu give per-directory trees and zdu reports faster runs than dust on its own trees.
verified_claims_summary: First-party hyperfine runs on the author's unnamed 8-core laptop over a private 15 GB folder (100k directories, 400k files): cold cache (drop_caches before each run) diskus 1.746 s vs du -sh 17.776 s (10.18x), warm cache 500.3 ms vs 1098.3 ms (2.20x, despite the prose saying more than 3x); CPU model, disk, filesystem, du version and diskus version are not stated.
status_note: Maintained by the author of fd and hyperfine (v0.9.0, last commit 2026-02-14, 1.3k stars), dual MIT/Apache-2.0 and widely packaged; the deep-tree stack overflow (#27) is still open.
